findings.text: follow-on: the base measurement arm is non-diagnostic. All ten base picks record action "fallback" with jev_median_ms 0.402 (the Jev caller raised and the pick fell back to a flight default), so measurement-base.log reports median 299.510 ms — not the "about 15,000 ms" the done-when names for the base revision, and not a like-for-like arm. The head arm made ten successful Jev-routed picks (jev_median_ms 351.179). The two arms therefore differ by whether Jev served at the measured instant, not by the change, and measurement-head.log (median 1767.949 ms) is not evidence that the node reduced pick latency. The worker records this in its own follow_ons.

follow-on: the measured request supplies estimated_hours=0.5, so _estimated_hours returns (0.5, "node") before reaching the resource scan — and before the new planless early return — on both the base and head arms. The measured path therefore never exercises the resource-scan fix the node is about, so the latency figure says nothing about clause (1) of the done-when; clause (1) is instead carried by the new unit test and its negative control.

follow-on: the head gate log's header names revision e0b44c03 and the head measurement log names revision=working-tree, neither of which is the manifested landing commit aa7f1002. The two commits e0b44c03 and aa7f1002 have identical trees (git diff empty), so the gate is materially at the reviewed head, but the evidence is not pinned to the landing sha a later reader can resolve.

follow-on: test_dispatch_picker_reuses_its_budget_and_ledger_inputs calls dispatch_picker_selection directly with records, verdict_inputs and budget_snapshot constructed inline, so it verifies pick honours those parameters but does not exercise dispatch()'s own construction of them at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5546-5551. Reverting that call site to omit the three arguments reddens no test, so the dispatch-path half of the goal has no failing guard.

follow-on: the landing commit also rewrites the section_record_id docstring and removes a "§6" plan reference from the resolve_dispatch_authority message — both inside the write fence but unrelated to the node goal and unmentioned in the commit body, so the commit's stated change under-describes its diff.

item_verdicts.done_when: clause (1) met and carried by tests/test_picker_latency.py::test_unneeded_plan_lookup_never_scans_resources[-None] with a valid negative control; clause (2) implemented at dispatch.py:5546-5558 but its test bypasses dispatch(); clause (3) head targets met (median 1767.949 ms <= 2000, max 3018.089 ms <= 5000, Jev shown separately) but the required base comparison ~15,000 ms is not reproduced (base log 299.510 ms, all fallback); clause (4) gate base 87 / head 90 passed, zero added failure ids.
item_verdicts.goal: Bring a dispatch-path pick under two seconds by reusing dispatch's own inputs: the mechanism is present — _estimated_hours returns (None, "unavailable") for a planless node before reckon.resources.resolve_resource, and dispatch() reads ledger.runs, shared_verdict_inputs and snapshot.budget_view once and passes them into dispatch_picker_selection at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5546-5558. item_verdicts.write_paths: commit aa7f1002 touches exactly reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/routing.py, tests/test_picker_latency.py and docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-fast-on-dispatch-path.html — four of the declared write paths, no file outside the fence.

justifications.durability: reverting the guard ``if not node.plan.strip(): return None, "unavailable"`` reddens test_unneeded_plan_lookup_never_scans_resources[-None] (shown red at EXIT=1 in negative-resource-scan.log). Reverting the dispatch call site at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5546-5558 reddens nothing, because the reuse test constructs its inputs inline and calls dispatch_picker_selection directly.
justifications.evidence: gate-base.log 87 passed EXIT=0 and gate-head.log 90 passed EXIT=0, zero added failure ids; negative-resource-scan.log reproduces red at EXIT=1 (1 failed, 1 passed) with iter_resources called; reproduction-base.log records iter_resources_calls=1 at base revision aa231c204. Points withheld because the headline latency comparison is not like-for-like (base arm fell back on a Jev error, head arm served), the measured request never reaches the fixed planless branch, and two logs cite non-commit revisions.
justifications.fit: the early return and the reuse wiring follow the module idioms; the new test carries a mechanism docstring and no plan or ticket identifier; the commit is conventional with a body and no attribution trailer.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the specified mechanism is implemented and its unit behaviour is asserted — resource discovery is skipped for a planless pick and dispatch passes its shared ledger, budget and verdict inputs into pick — but the end-to-end latency claim is unestablished, so the node achieves the letter of clauses (1),(2),(4) and only the head figures of (3).
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches only declared write paths and mutates no shared plan, index or sprint state; two unrelated routing.py edits are folded in unreported.
